results.title: Congressional Baseball Team Managers Vow Game Will Go Ahead : CSPAN : June 15, 2017 4:12am-4:48am EDT
results.description: Representatives Joe Barton (R-TX) and Mike Doyle (D-PA) held a news conference in the wake of the shooting of Representative Steve Scalise (R-LA) at a baseball practice in Alexandria, Virginia. They announced that the Congressional Baseball Game, for which Republicans were practicing during the shooting, would still occur the following day. They also answered questions regarding security at the upcoming game and on the condition of some of the victims. People: Joe Barton; Mike Doyle Sponsor: U.S. Capitol | House Radio and Television Gallery

results.description: One day, sometime in the eighteenth century, the attention of a certain Frenchman, Francois Marie de Arouet, was directed to a case which first shook a town, then France, and finally Europe: the murder of Jean Calais, a Protestant merchant of Toulouse. The Catholic Church had accused Calais of hanging one of his sons to prevent his becoming a Catholic, “as it was the common practice amongst Protestants. ” Calais was arrested, and the civil magistrates ecclesiastical orders—condemned the old man to the rack, to be broken alive upon the wheel and then to be burned to ashes. This decree was executed on March 9, 1762. F. M. de Arouet dedicated the best part of three years to proving Calas’s complete innocence, which he did. Simultaneously he swore to wage relentless war against a church which was capable of such murderous intolerance. Having coined a slogan, Ecrasez l’infame, he used it in all his books, articles, letters. His one-man campaign eventually contributed, perhaps more than any other, to the overthrow of Catholic encroachment upon civil authority in France, and, indeed, in most of Europe in the decades to come. Francois Marie de Arouet’s other name: Voltaire. One day, also in the same century, a certain Roger Williams, while passing through Springfield Green in the North American colonies, saw a youth of fourteen being burned at the stake by the civil magistrates, under orders of the Church of England. Roger Williams swore to fight to the utmost the Protestant church which had enjoined civil authority to enforce her religious tyranny. Voltaire in Europe and Roger Williams in America, by openly revolting against Catholic and Protestant intolerance, had personified the will of the old and new worlds to get rid of all ecclesiastical encroachment upon civil authority. Catholic Power today, as yesterday and tomorrow, has one supreme objective: the Catholicization of the human race. To attain this, the Catholic Church will suffer no obstacles, be deterred by no barriers, tolerate no enemies, rivals, competitors, or even friends. Her clarion call to Ecumenism, reunion and Unity is nothing but a specious screen behind which to hide such millenarian ambition. It cannot be otherwise. Her aim has never changed in the past, does not change in the present, and will change less in the future. What has changed now is her strategy, her tactics, her methods, her approach, her parlance, and her seeming acceptance of modern liberties. Neither her revolutionary innovations nor the individual humanity or intellectual liberality of some of her latest Popes can obliterate the central fact that she considers herself divinely inspired, divinely commissioned, and divinely predestined to Catholicize the world. His book is warning of a danger, and a threat for the generations yet to come, a nightmarish omen for the future of mankind. Baron Avro Manhattan was born April 6, 1914, in Milan, Italy, of American and Swiss/Dutch parents. He was educated at the Sorbonne in Paris and the London School of Economics. results.title: Indian & English dictionary
creator: Swan, Bradford F. (Bradford Fuller) fmo RIBRL
Rhode Island Historical Society. Library. fmo RIBRL
description: Ms. codex
Title taken from ms. slip of covers of volumes 1-3
Dates of publication suggested by JCB Catalogue of manuscript codices

Originally made up of eight volumes, this manuscript Indian and English dictionary consists of four surviving volumes. Based on an extensive compilation process in which terms for various North American Indian languages were collected from different sources. The sources used included A key into the language of America / by Roger Williams, first printed in 1643, with words in the Narragansett language, designated as "RW" in the manuscript, a list of Nanticoke terms labeled as "Nan" and other lists as yet unidentified, labeled as "A", "B", "C", "H", "L", "S", "W", and "Z"

Dictionary entries were written on lined paper and then cut out as individual slips and pasted onto the pages of unrelated printed books in an alphabetical arrangement, forming an attempt at a comprehensive dictionary of Indian and English terms, probably limited to Algonquian languages used in the northeastern United States

Volume 1 has 142 pages and consists of entries Aa to Me; the papers are pasted on the sheets of volume 2 of The history of the wars which arose out of the French Revolution to which is prefixed, a review of the causes of that event / by Alexander Stephens, Philadelphia, 1804. This volume retains its title page, is bound in full contemporary mottled calf and measures 22 cm. tall

Volume 2 has p. 171-359 and consists of entries Me to Wa; the papers are pasted on sheets made up from a German hymnbook. This volume is bound in contemporary full mottled calf and measures 18 cm. tall

Volume 3 has p. 360-421 and consists of entries Wa to Zed, and a supplementary list for entried Ach to Yu, on p. 422-447; the papers are pasted on sheets made up from a German theological text. This volume is bound in contemprary full mottled calf and measures 17 cm. tall
Volumes 1-3 are housed in three cream cloth covered phase boxes with volumes 3 and 4 being housed together; the phase boxes measure 25 cm. tall
John Carter Brown Library copy acquired from the estate of Bradford F. Swan
Provenance of the John Carter Brown Library copy: Rhode Island Historical Society: book stamps on front pastedowns

results.title: Pegasus 5.0
results.creator: Starcom
results.description: Die Pegasus 5.0 CDROM bietet Ihnen eine Sammlung von internationalen Shareware und Public-Domain Programmen. Als Zusatz gibt es eine Multimedia-Bonus-CDROM für Windows. (Alle Pegasus-CDROMs enthalten über 650 MB der aktuellsten und besten deutschen und internationalen Shareware-Programme. Die Auswahl der Programme erfolgte von einem Kenner der Shareware-Szene. Alle Dateibeschreibungen in Deutsch. Zwei Menüsysteme für DOS und Windows erlauben das automatische Entpacken und Kopieren der Dateien, Starten der Programme, Lesen von Textdateien und vieles mehr. FILES.BBS für den sofortigen Mailbox-Einsatz. Die unterschiedlichen Versionen der Pegasus-CDROMs enthalten so gut wie keine Duplikate von Programmen. Mit dieser Serie besitzen Sie somit eine der bestsortiertesten Shareware-Sammlungen der Welt.) TRADEWRK.ZIP 2813323 06-10-94 Tradework for Windows 1.0 ist eine Auftragsbearbeitung vom Feinsten. Besonders übersichtlich und einfach zu bedienen. Tradework ist eine Auftragsbearbeitung vom Feinsten. Besonderer Wert wurde auf Übersichtlichkeit und einfache Bedienung gelegt. Der Funktionsumfang von Tradework umfaß folgende Möglichkeiten: Angebote erfassen und daraus Aufträge generieren, Bestellwesen, Direkterfassung von Bestellungen und Aufträgen, Kunden- und Lieferantenverwaltung, Artikelverwaltung und Lagerführung, Mahnwesen, Umsatzstatistiken, offene Posten Kontrolle, Etikettendruck uvm. ANAGRA15.ZIP 77715 06-03-94 Anagrams v1.5, bildet aus einem Wort alle möglichen Buchstabenkombinationen Bildet anhand eines festen (englischen!) Wortschatzes ein Anagram (Buchstabenpuzzle) zu einem vorgebenen Wort oder Satz. Mit vielen Optionen zur Beeinflussung des Ergebnisses und relativ umfangreicher Dokumentationsdatei. ARZTPW.ZIP 1222995 12-06-94 Arztpraxis Wiegand, umfangreiches Verwaltungsprogramm für die Arztpraxis, relativ leistungsfähig (deutsch) Verwaltungsprogramm für Arztpraxen. Alle anfallenden Vorgänge von der Stammdatenerfassung für jeden Patienten über das Ausstellen von Mahnungen bis zum Quartalsabschluß können damit automatisiert werden. Zusätzlich lassen sich beliebige Datenbanken mit Patientendaten, Medikamenten usw. anlegen. Für Datensicherung sorgt eine automatische Back-Up-Funktion und eine Paßwort-Option. Verschiedene AddOn´s sind verfügbar, wie eine Dateienverwaltung für Hausbesuche und die Gelbe Liste Pharmindex (kostet DM 100 extra). Regelmäßige Updates zu Beginn eines jeden Quartals. BALG20.ZIP 116922 12-02-94 Basic Algebra v2.0, Algebra-Lernprogramm für Kinder und Erwachsene Einfaches Lern- und Übungsprogramm zum Training der Rechenfähigkeit. Auf erklärende Texte zu verschiedenen Themengebieten folgen Testaufgaben. Die Erfolgsquote wird sofort ermittelt und anschließend grafisch dargestellt. Der Lernstoff von Basic Algebra beschränkt sich auf die unterschiedlichen Zahlenarten, auf Brüche und Gleichungen. Das Programm führt übrigens bei jedem Programmstart einen automatischen Viren-Check durch. BEAM21.ZIP 49144 01-03-94 Beam v2.1, simple Statikberechnung von diversen Stahlträgerprofilen Programm zur Berechnung der statischen Eigenschaften von Trägerprofilen unterschiedlicher Ausmaße und Materialien. Alle relevanten Eigenschaften der Träger sind berücksichtigt und können vorgegeben werden. Das Tool ist Teil der umfangreichen Sammlung von Engineers Shareware (insgesamt über 60 Tools), die weitere Hilfsmittel für Berechnungen am Bau enthält (Registrierungsgebühr hierfür: US$ 195). CAMP_D.ZIP 159966 09-05-94 Camping in Deutschland v94/04, elektronischer Campingführer, gibt nach Kriterien bestimmte Campingplätze in Deutschland aus (deutsch) Elektronischer Campingführer für ganz Deutschland. Alle wichtigen Daten zur Beurteilung der Eignung eines Platzes sind vorhanden: Lage, Ausstattung, Serviceleistungen, mögliche Lärmbelästigungen, Nutzungsbedingungen (auf manchen Campingplätzen dürfen z.B. keine Caravans aufgestellt werden) und die ungefähre Preislage. Daneben erleichtert das Programm die Routenplanung und bietet die Möglichkeit, zu jedem Eintrag eigene Notizen zu machen. Eine Suchfunktion ist ebenfalls vorhanden. (Die Shareware-Version enthält nur Einträge aus dem Saarland und Schleswig-Holstein.) CAMP_F.ZIP 141220 22-04-94 Camping in Frankreich v94/04, elektronischer Campingführer, gibt nach Kriterien bestimmte Campingplätze in Frankreich aus (deutsch) Elektronischer Campingführer für Frankreich. Alle wichtigen Daten zur Beurteilung der Eignung eines Platzes sind vorhanden: Lage, Ausstattung, Serviceleistungen, mögliche Lärmbelästigungen, Nutzungsbedingungen (auf manchen Campingplätzen dürfen z.B. keine Caravans aufgestellt werden) und die ungefähre Preislage. Daneben erleichtert das Programm die Routenplanung und bietet die Möglichkeit, zu jedem Eintrag eigene Notizen zu machen. CIDFIN55.ZIP 630734 11-06-94 CID Finanzbuchhaltung v5.5, netzwerkfähiges Buchhaltungsprogramm für Klein- und Mittelstandsbetriebe (deutsch), vernünftig aufgebaut Ein branchenunabhäniges Finanzbuchaltungsprogramm, das für kleine und mittelständische Betriebe völlig ausreichend ist. Neben dem eigentlichen Buchhaltungstool stehen ein Programm Kostenrechnung, eine Versionskennung und verschiedene Mustertexte und -formulare (z.B. für Mahnungen oder Kontoauszüge). Das Programm ist in deutscher Sprache und übersichtlich aufgebaut. Für den Einsatz in einem Netzwerk (Novell Netware) ist keine spezielle Netzwerk-Version notwendig, sondern lediglich weitere Einzellizenzen. Die Testphase ist auf 60 Tage limitiert. Zur Vollversion gehört ein gedrucktes Handbuch und Lehrbuch. CL_23.ZIP 412984 15-03-94 Contact-Lens v2.3, Kontakt-Management-Software, für jeden, der viel Kontakte/Geschäftsbeziehungen per Telefon unterhält Ein Personal Information Manager, der bei der Verwaltung und Speicherung von Terminen, Adressen, Kontakten und persönlichen Notizen hilft. Die angelegten Datenbanken können nach 22 Kriterien durchsucht werden. Datenbestände im dBase-Format können importiert werden. Eigene Daten lassen sich ebenso in dieses Format exportieren. Auch Report- und Druckfunktionen stehen zur Verfügung. Die Testversion ist auf 30 Tage limitiert. CNVRT48.ZIP 82804 11-03-94 Conversion of Units v4.08, kommandozeilengesteuertes Umrechnungsprogramm für eine Vielzahl verschiedenster Maßeinheiten Ein kleines Konvertierungstool. Maße, Gewichte und Währungen werden in beliebige andere Einheiten derselben Kategorie umgerechnet. Auch durch Wechselkursschwankungen oder andere Änderungen veraltet das Programm nicht, da sich die Umrechnungsfaktoren manipulieren lassen. CODEGEN.ZIP 85834 05-03-94 Code to Graphics Generator v1.0, Trainingstool für CNC-Programmierer, relativ umfangreich Umfangreiches Trainingsprogramm für CNC-Programmierer, kein ausgesprochenes Lernprogramm. Statt dessen werden für verschiedene, immer wiederkehrende Programmier-Aufgaben Lösungsstrategien angeboten. Der Hersteller bietet ausdrücklich Support bei Problemen mit dem Programm. Bei 386er-CPUs wird ein mathematischer Co-Prozessor empfohlen. CONVERT1.ZIP 87217 01-03-94 Convert v1.0, Umrechnen zwischen den gängigsten Maßeinheiten Sehr einfaches Umwandlungsprogramm für einige wenige Maßeinheiten (Temperaturen, Entfernungen usw.). Problematische Bedienung, unflexible Oberfläche. CSHFL351.ZIP 469776 15-01-94 Up your Cash Flow v3.5.1, umfangreiches Finanzplanungsprogramm (Profit/Loss, Cash-Flow errechnen...) Finanzplanungsprogramm, daß Ein- und Ausgaben eines Privathaushaltes in übersichtlicher Tabellenform darstellt. Geplante Ausgaben lassen sich in Beziehung zum erwarteten Einkommen setzen, Sparpläne könnnen aufgestellt werden und außerdem liefert das Programm 50 Tips zur persönlichen Geldanlage (diese natürlich orientiert an amerikanische Bedingungen). Zusätzlich zur Registrierungsgebühr werden US$ 15 Versandkosten fällig. Die Version ist limitiert auf 30 Tage. DEMOS401.ZIP 374601 08-01-94 The Demo System v4.01, entwerfen von eigenen Text-Slideshows, z.B. für Präsentationen (viele Optionen) Programm zum Entwerfen einfacher Präsentationen. Eines der Module captured einzelne Screens (nur Textscreens mit 80 Zeichen und 25 Zeilen), ein anderes fügt sie zusammen und produziert daraus eine selbstlaufende Slideshow, die etwa zu Präsentationszwecken genutzt werden kann. Zum Programmpaket gehören noch einige Tools zur Textgestaltung, z.B. Fonts und ein Font-Generator. DTA100.ZIP 287924 01-03-94 DTA v1.0, Erstellen von Disketten zum Datenträgeraustausch mit der Bank (deutsch) Erstellt Bankdisketten für den elektronischen Zahlungsverkehr mit der Bank mit komfortabler SAA-Oberläche. Alle alltäglichen Vorgänge, wie Überweisungen, Lastschriften oder Einziehungen lassen sich automatisieren. Häufig wiederkehrende Daten von Zahlungsempfängern o.a. (also Kontonummern, Adressen usw.) könnnen in einer kleinen Datenbank abgelegt und bei Bedarf abgerufen werden. EEDLIB10.ZIP 16675 15-01-94 EEDLib v1.0, zusätzliche Bibliothek für das Elektronik-CAD-Programm EEDraw, enthält hauptsächlich ICs Eine Bibliothek mit Zusätzen für das auf Elektronik-Design spezialisierte CAD-Programm EEDraw (Freeware, Autor: Gershon Elber). Die Sammlung enthält u.a. die am weitesten verbreiteten CPUs und MPUs, ICs, Dioden, Induktoren und verwandte Bauteile. Voraussetzung ist das Vorhandensein von EEDraw. ENERGY20.ZIP 264951 17-01-94 Energy Cost v2.0, hilft herauszufinden, wie man bei Lampen am meisten Energie sparen kann (welche Lampen verwenden...) Ein Öko-Programm, daß helfen kann, Energiekosten zu analysieren und damit auch zu senken. Es berechnet nach Eingabe der entsprechenden Parameter den aktuellen Energieverbrauch und zeigt Möglichkeiten auf, durch den Einsatz alternativer Technologien und umweltgerechter Produkte Energie (und Geld!) zu sparen. Limitiert auf 30 Tage. EUROCAMP.ZIP 608559 22-04-94 Euro-Camp v1/2, elektronischer Campingführer, gibt nach Kriterien bestimmte Campingplätze in Europa aus (deutsch) Elektronischer Campingführer durch Westeuropa. Alle wichtigen Daten zur Beurteilung der Eignung eines Platzes sind vorhanden: Lage, Ausstattung, Serviceleistungen, mögliche Lärmbelästigungen, Nutzungsbedingungen (auf manchen Campingplätzen dürfen z.B. keine Caravans aufgestellt werden) und die ungefähre Preislage. Andersherum können auch die Anforderungen an einen Campingplatz definiert werden und das Programm sucht etwas passendes aus. In diesem Programm sind Camping und Deutschland sowie Camping in Frankreich als Module enthalten (s. CAMP_D.ZIP und CAMP_F.ZIP). GASTRO10.ZIP 246378 10-01-94 Gastro-Kalkulation v1.0, Kalkulation von Zutaten bei der Erstellung von Gerichten in Zusammenhang mit Ein- und Verkaufspreis (deutsch) Ein Kalkulationprogramm mit SAA-Oberfläche vor allem für die professionelle Küche. Die für die Zubereitung eines Gerichtes benötigten Waren und Zutaten pro Portion können nach Einkaufspreis, Einsatzmenge und Verkaufspreis des Einzelgerichtes erfaßt und die ermittelten Daten ausgewertet werden. Ergänzt wird das Programm durch eine Rezept- und Zutaten-Datenbank. Auf gängigen Druckern (Epson, HP) lassen sich die verschiedenen Daten auch zu Papier bringen. GCAT31WP.ZIP 109858 20-06-94 GraphCat v3.1, Katalogsystem, hilft dabei, WordPerfect 5.1/6.0-Cliparts zu katalogisieren, leicht zu bedienen Mit diesem Katalogisierungs-Tool lassen sich Cliparts erfassen, in eine sinnvolle Ordnung bringen und schließlich verwalten. results.description: Die Pegasus 5.0 CDROM bietet Ihnen eine Sammlung von internationalen Shareware und Public-Domain Programmen. Als Zusatz gibt es eine Multimedia-Bonus-CDROM für Windows. (Alle Pegasus-CDROMs enthalten über 650 MB der aktuellsten und besten deutschen und internationalen Shareware-Programme. Die Auswahl der Programme erfolgte von einem Kenner der Shareware-Szene. FILES.BBS für den sofortigen Mailbox-Einsatz. Die unterschiedlichen Versionen der Pegasus-CDROMs enthalten so gut wie keine Duplikate von Programmen. Mit dieser Serie besitzen Sie somit eine der bestsortiertesten Shareware-Sammlungen der Welt.) TRADEWRK.ZIP 2813323 06-10-94 Tradework for Windows 1.0 ist eine Auftragsbearbeitung vom Feinsten. Besonders übersichtlich und einfach zu bedienen. Tradework ist eine Auftragsbearbeitung vom Feinsten. Besonderer Wert wurde auf Übersichtlichkeit und einfache Bedienung gelegt. Der Funktionsumfang von Tradework umfaß folgende Möglichkeiten: Angebote erfassen und daraus Aufträge generieren, Bestellwesen, Direkterfassung von Bestellungen und Aufträgen, Kunden- und Lieferantenverwaltung, Artikelverwaltung und Lagerführung, Mahnwesen, Umsatzstatistiken, offene Posten Kontrolle, Etikettendruck uvm. Alle anfallenden Vorgänge von der Stammdatenerfassung für jeden Patienten über das Ausstellen von Mahnungen bis zum Quartalsabschluß können damit automatisiert werden. Zusätzlich lassen sich beliebige Datenbanken mit Patientendaten, Medikamenten usw. anlegen. Für Datensicherung sorgt eine automatische Back-Up-Funktion und eine Paßwort-Option. Das Programm führt übrigens bei jedem Programmstart einen automatischen Viren-Check durch. THINKER3.ZIP 106482 25-05-94 Thinker v3.0, Clone/Abart des Farben-Knobelspiels Master Mind, hier müssen jedoch Symbole erraten werden Abwandlung des bekannten Knobelspiels Master Mind, bei dem Farbkombinationen zu erraten sind. WHEEL11.ZIP 164431 26-05-94 Wheel of Luck v1.1, Umsetzung der Dauerwerbe-Fernsehshow Glücksrad (aber wenigstens ohne dümmliche Moderatoren) Des Deutschen liebstes Kind (oder zumindest eines der liebsten Kinder) dürfte Glücksrad sein, das Dauerwerbespiel, bei dem Begriffe geraten werden müssen. Da das Spiel ursprünglich aus den USA kommt, wundert es auch nicht, daß die Windows-Umsetzung ebenfalls aus den USA kommt. Nunja, wer´s mag... WININST.ZIP 818220 01-05-94 Win-Install v3.63, sehr gutes und umfangreiches Installationsutility für beliebige Applikationen (deutsch) Win-Install ist ein Werkzeug, mit dem Sie Ihre selbst geschriebenen Programme auf einfache Weise und ohne eine Scriptsprache erlernen zu müssen für den Vertrieb fertig auf Diskette(n) portieren können. TURNIER1.ZIP 877427 06-05-94 ro-Turnier v1.0, umfangreiche und leistungsföhige Turnierverwaltung für Windows (deutsch) ro-Turnier ist ein Turnier-Verwaltungsprogramm anläßlich der Fußball-WM 1994, mit dem sich bis zu 99 Turniere verwalten lassen. Je Turnier sind 64 Mannschaften möglich, und jede Mannschaft darf 30 Spieler umfassen. Im Lieferumfang des Programms sind die Ergebnisse aller bisher stattgefundenen WM´s enthalten, auch alle Nationalflaggen sind enthalten. WBASE15.ZIP 1290022 06-05-94 WinBase v1.5, leistungsfähige Windows-Datenbank mit freier Formular- und Berichtgestaltung (deutsch) Leistungsstarke Windows-Datenbank mit freier Formular-, Etiketten- und Berichtgestaltung; Einbindung von Feldern mehrerer Dateien, Tabellenfeldern, Formelfeldern, Bildfeldern, Bilddateien, Schriftarten; Formatierung und Überprüfung von Eingaben. Gestaltung mit interaktivem Layoutdesigner. Druck von Serienbriefen. Darstellung der Daten in From von Masken und frei konfiguierbaren Tabellen. xBASE-kompatibel, Memo-, Bild-, Externfelder. Einfachste Bedienung, über 150 xBASE-Funktionen und über 100 xBASE-Befehle. Ausführen von xBASE-Programmen. Verbinden von bis zu 10 geöffneten Dateien, Datenaustausch über Zwischenablage und DDE, Import/Export, ideale Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Programmen. Durch Externfelder auch als Dokumentenverwaltung einsetzbar. Interaktives oder formelgestütztes Selektieren von Daten, wiederverwendbare Abfragen. Arbeitsmappen zum automatischen Öffnen und Verbinden von Datenbankdateien. STRAINER.ZIP 499165 17-05-94 Ihr Schreibtrainer v3.2, sehr guter und umfangreicher Schreibmaschinentrainer (deutsch) Der Schreibtrainer ist ein Lernprogramm für´s 10-Finger-System auf deutschen Tastaturen. In dieser wird von links nach rechts der Übungstext mit einem bestimmten Tempo durchgeschoben. TASKER11.ZIP 61659 12-03-94 Tasker v1.1, einfacher, icongesteuerter Taskswitcher, schaltet nur zwischen den aktiven Applikationen um Ein einfacher, icongesteuerter Taskswitcher, dessen einzige Funktion darin besteht, zwischen den laufenden Applikationen hin- und herzuschalten. TASKIT11.ZIP 554309 21-04-94 Task-It v1.1, Taskmanager, Programmstarter per Iconfeld, Speicher-Optimierer und System-Information in einer Applikation vereint Dies ist ein kombinieter Taskmanager und Programmstarter per Iconfeld. TIMR12.ZIP 225861 24-02-94 Break Timer v1.2, kleiner Wecker, der daran erinnert, auch mal eine Pause zu machen Break Timer ist ein kleiner Wecker, der in definierbaren Abständen daran erinnert, auch mal eine Pause zu machen. UNINST15.ZIP 374341 07-07-94 S.I.P. Uninstall v1.5, überwacht Aktionen von Installationsprogrammen unter Windows, gestattet vollständige DeInstallation (deutsch) S.I.P. UNZIPF11.ZIP 15234 29-09-93 UnZip FrontEnd v1.1, einfache Shell für den Packer PkZIP, erleichtert das Auspacken von ZIP-Archiven UnZip FrontEnd ist eine einfache Shell für den Packer PkUnzip, es erleichtert das Auspacken von ZIP-Archiven. USAGE11.ZIP 11288 04-01-94 Computer Usage Log v1.1, hilft dabei zu überwachen, wie viel Zeit man am Rechner für bestimmte Aufgaben verbraucht Computer Usage Log hilft dabei zu überwachen, wie viel Zeit man am Rechner für bestimmte Aufgaben verbraucht. WYWO42.ZIP 189025 21-07-94 While you were out v4.2, Nachrichten auf dem Desktop hinterlassen, auch in Netzwerken While you were out ist ein kleines Utility, daß es Ihnen erlaubt, Nachrichten auf dem Desktop für Zeiten Ihrer Abwesenheit zu hinterlassen, funktioniert auch in Netzwerken. YACC101.ZIP 27245 24-04-94 Yet another Clipboad Collector v1.01, verwaltet den Inhalt des Clipboards, so daß dort mehrere Dateien abgelegt werden können Dies ist eine Erweiterung der Windows-Zwischenablage. YEAH40.ZIP 259820 03-03-94 Yeah! v4.0, Ressourcenmonitor etc. als kompaktes kleines Fenster, gut bedienbar Ein Ressourcenmonitor, der noch eine ganze Reihe anderer Eigenschaften hat, die den Umgang mit Windows vereinfachen. YWA10.ZIP 3371 10-03-94 You WIN again v1.0, schneller Neustart von Windows Die Ausführung von You WIN again verursacht einen schnellen Neustart von Windows, z.B. nach der Änderung von INI-Dateien, die erst nach einem solchen Neustart wirksam werden. ZHRMET.ZIP 65664 18-03-94 Win Hour-Meter v1.0, findet heraus, wie viele Stunden Windows seit dessen Installation betrieben wurde Dieses Utility findet heraus, wie viele Stunden Windows seit dessen Installation betrieben wurde (warum auch immer...) ZIPNAV20.ZIP 638293 01-06-94 ZIP-Navigator v2.0, Bedienoberfläche für das Archivprogramm PkZIP, etwas gewöhnungsbedürftig in der Bedienung Eine Bedienoberfläche für das Archivprogramm PkZIP, das allerdings etwas gewöhnungsbedürftig in der Bedienung ist. ZIPVIEW1.ZIP 247590 30-01-94 ZIP Viewer v1.0, Betrachten von ZIP-Archiven per Drag & Drop vom Dateimanager aus Der ZIP Viewer erlaubt das Betrachten von ZIP-Archiven per Drag&Drop-Technik direkt vom Windows-Dateimanager aus. results.title: Lillian Johnson Scrapbook, 1929-1972, Volume 1 of 2
results.creator: Johnson, Lillian
description: Please visit the California Revealed website to see the most complete and up-to-date version of this object: https://californiarevealed.org/node/339259 .
Object consists of disbound scrapbook pages rehoused within a portfolio album.

Please be advised that this scrapbook contains language, specifically the word “midget”, which, in the view of Little People of America, is offensive and inappropriate. This scrapbook shows events from before Little People of America called for the abolishment of the word in 2015, and it is the view of Little People of America that this object has historical significance despite the use of the word. The word was never coined as the official term to identify people with dwarfism, but was created as a label used to refer to people of short stature who were on public display for curiosity and sport. Today, the word is considered a derogatory slur. The dwarfism community has voiced that they prefer to be referred to as dwarfs, little people, people of short stature or having dwarfism, or simply, and most preferably, by their given name.

Lillian Johnson, the creator of this scrapbook, was a dwarf, pituitary type, who formed a chapter of Little People of America with her husband in Sacramento, California. She could be described as a proportional dwarf, as her body and extremities were proportional like the general population, but she was short. Her adult height was 4 feet, 4 inches. She was born in Texas in 1929, where she obtained a high school education, but was not able to find employment. She left Texas when she was 21 and joined a circus. While working in the circus, she met her future husband and together they had a show business career for several years. During World War II, her husband began working at Lockheed Aircraft in Long Beach, California. After the war, they worked as custodians on a large cattle ranch near Bakersfield. In her daily life, she shopped for the family and cooked meals, while her husband took care of maintenance and repair. They moved to Sacramento where her husband went to work as a Jet Engine Mechanic at McClellan Air Force Base. He later trained for Radio and TV repair and set up shop in his home. In 1957, she and her husband attended the founding meeting of Little People of America, held in Reno, Nevada in 1957. After that meeting, they formed a chapter in Sacramento and were active in LPA. Following her husband’s death, she moved to Bakersfield where she died in 1993. Sprinkled throughout the scrapbooks are news articles, featuring Lillian and her husband, that chronicle and document their travels and their volunteer work for LPA.

Contents include: Inside front cover - photo of Lillian Johnson and brief biography, 1929 - Midget Circus opens in Dallas, Texas, Circus closes in San Antonio, Texas, 1931 - flyer announcing Midget Actors at Municipal Auditorium, 1936 - news article discussing Tom Thumb and P. T. Barnum, 1944 - Martin "Shorty" Daly shows off his new drinking fountain stool at Douglas Aircraft, Brownie Rogers rivets airplane fuselage at Willow Run Ford Plant, 1945 - Angelo Rossitto and Georgia Burash Wed, Ann Renna and Floyd Dixon Wed, George Liable retires from the circus, Waylon Galloway and Mary Copeland of Burbank, marry, 1948 - Richard Mackey, 4 feet 7 inches, is enlisted in U.S. Air Force, Odette Pilkerton and Joseph Katalik are wed in Ashley, Pennsylvania, 1949 - George Havens and Jeanette McGill Marry, Ovitz family of dwarfs in Haifa, Israel, Trinidad Milano gives birth to Mary Ann in Cleveland, Ohio, 1950 - Pygmy Island Film is planned, Johnsons in Hibbing, Minnesota, Marion Nichols and Betty Millican marry, Waino Johnson as Clown at children’s party, Marion Nichols at Lockheed Blood Drive, discussion of Pituitary Dwarfism and Genetics, Maria Spada of Turin, Italy, 33" tall, gives birth to a son.1951 - TV creates shortage of midgets, 1954 - Birth of Debra Dixon in Los Angeles, Maria Spada, Turin Italy, 33" tall is expecting second child, 1957 - Reno Meeting - Founding of LPA, Waino and Lilliam interviewed by Sacramento paper, Sacramento Bee runs story and photo of Tom Thumb visit to Sacramento in 1877, 1959 - Billy Barty prepares gift for Peter Gunn, 1959 - Buster and Hazel Rezmondo, stand-ins for child actors discuss their life, 1961 - Lillian and Waino Johnson in Sacramento, California, photo and story of Lillian and Waino Johnson prior to attending the 1961 LPA convention in Las Vegas, Marriage of Vivian Gant and Kenneth Nichols in Seattle, Washington, 1963 - Little People claim job discrimination in films and the beginning of Association of Little People, 1964 - convention in Phoenix, Arizona, fashion show in Phoenix, newlyweds George and Tina Boehm, and the Maury Alden's who their wedding ensembles, Len Garman and Aileen Henderson marry in Gardena, California, carnival sideshow workers share their lifestyle and work patterns from Gibsonton, Florida, photo of Howsden twins at District 12 convention in Bakersfield, California, John Clifton of Buster Brown Shoes 1965 - LPA Convention in Gloucester, N.J., Bob Spector talks about his lifestyle as a dwarf, Lee Wright and Robert Anderson talk about 1966 Convention to be held in Austin, Texas, photo and story of Lillian and Waino reported by Sacramento Bee, Michael Dunn talks about "Ship of Fools", 1966 - photos and captions of LPA members who attended the Austin, Texas convention, photo and caption of District 12 convention in Fresno, California, photo and story of Frieda Groenveld first grade teacher in Darrington, Washington, Bob East and Billy Barty at District 12 convention in Fresno, California, 1967 - Fred "Shorty" Roberts - Constable in Yazoo City, Mississippi, G.C. Simmons talks about LPA in District 8, Lee Kitchens talks about LPA Convention in Hollywood, California, Scott Lau of Sacramento begins treatment for Pituitary Dwarfism and experiences a growth spurt, 9 Little People/entertainers live at the Harvey Hotel in Los Angeles, Johnny Lucas, valet to Russian Prince dies in Chicago, 1968 - District 8 conference in Lubbock, Texas, Billy Curtis talks about Little People and casting of Planet of the Apes and how he got into acting, 1969 - San Francisco Bay Chapter hosts District conference in Concord.

results.title: Portrait of Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey, née Lamack
results.creator: John I Smart (British, 1741–1811)
description: Portrait of Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey, née Lamack, c. 1776. John I Smart (British, 1741–1811). Graphite and wash on laid paper in a modern gold frame; framed: 6.2 x 5.3 cm (2 7/16 x 2 1/16 in.); unframed: 5.8 x 4.8 cm (2 5/16 x 1 7/8 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Edward B. Greene Collection 1942.1155
Sketches helped John Smart work out the particulars of a portrait before commencing the miniature on ivory, and they were useful in the event that a duplicate might later be required.

Although it is impossible to say if it was always part of the artist’s process to execute a preparatory sketch prior to painting each miniature, we do know that John Smart retained many hundreds of these sketches. A group of preparatory sketches—of which this portrait is one—descended through the Smirke family after Smart’s daughter Sarah gave a sketchbook containing preparatory portrait studies to her friend Mary Smirke, sister of the celebrated Victorian architect Sydney Smirke. This book was probably broken up around 1877 when it was divided between Sydney’s daughters Mary Jemmett and Mrs. Lange, whose portions were both sold at auction in 1928. Compared to his contemporaries George Engleheart (1752–1829) and Andrew Plimer (1763–1837), whose female sitters were often painted in similar simple white gowns, Smart often lavished more attention on the costumes in his portraits of women, whose dresses incorporated colored silks, printed fabrics, and luxury trimmings like lace and fur, as seen in this portrait. Mrs. Bailey wears a violet surcoat trimmed with fur, worn over a cream-colored gown trimmed with a border of alternating pearls and blue stones and two vertical rows of pearls with one large pearl between them. Her brown hair is dressed high with ringlets descending down her neck and over her shoulders. The coiffure is ornamented with a strand of pearls and two ostrich plumes. The case is modern, and there is a brownish cast to what was originally pale, cream-colored paper—the result of light exposure changing the color over time. Smart’s preparatory sketches were compiled in books but once removed were often grouped in frames or placed in lockets such as this one. This portrait was part of the Smirke collection owned by Mary Jemmett, who sold it at Christie’s, London, on February 29, 1928. Lot 61 for this sale is described as “Mrs. Bailey, wearing pale mauve and white dress, her hair dressed high and trimmed with feathers.” The sitter, Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey (née Lamack), of Clapham, married the member of Parliament for Abingdon on March 18, 1773. Her husband was of sufficient means and is recorded in 1775 as having performed his annual distribution of £100 of bread and meat to the poor of his borough. Little else is known about this sitter. This drawing was a preparatory study for a portrait on ivory, signed and dated 1776, and measuring 2 inches high. The ivory miniature was formerly in the Ashcroft collection and was sold at Sotheby’s, London, in May 1946 to Arthur Jaffé, having previously been on loan to the Victoria and Albert Museum from 1924 to 1939. In this sale the miniature is described as “An Attractive Miniature of a Lady, by John Smart, signed and dated 1776, head and gaze three-quarters dexter, a white feather and pearls in her high piled chestnut hair, ringlets falling to the shoulders, wearing a pearl and emerald bordered low-cut cream dress and fur trimmed lavender jacket.” It most recently sold at Christie’s, London, in 2003. This portrait miniature is identical to the preparatory sketch here, both of which describe the sitter as wearing a faintly violet costume, though this color is no longer discernible in the sketch. The current location of the miniature on ivory is unknown. Edward Greene donated this and nine other preparatory studies by Smart to the Cleveland Museum of Art in 1941 and 1942. This sketch was acquired by Greene from Leopold Davis for around $260 in 1930. Although this portrait was probably part of the same sketchbook as the other nine purchased by Greene, Davis did not indicate whether or not this was indeed the case. The majority of these sketches were in a compromised condition, with fading and foxing especially prevalent.

results.title: Portrait of Sir Thomas Baring, 2nd Baronet
results.creator: George Engleheart (British, 1752–1829)
description: Portrait of Sir Thomas Baring, 2nd Baronet, 1803. George Engleheart (British, 1752–1829). Watercolor on ivory in a gilt metal frame with plaited brown hair in glazed reserve on back; framed: 8.6 x 7 cm (3 3/8 x 2 3/4 in.); unframed: 8 x 6.3 cm (3 1/8 x 2 1/2 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Edward B. Greene Collection 1942.1140
Engleheart also painted miniatures of Baring's wife and elder sons whose names are listed in the artists fee book; he was charging from 12 to 15 guineas for a miniature painting.

Though this portrait has had the title “Portrait of a Man” since 1942 when it entered the museum’s collection, the sitter was identified by previous owners, including Leo Schidlof and Edward Greene, as a member of the famous Baring banking family, of whom G. C. Williamson mentions several members in his biography of George Engleheart. Thomas Baring (1772–1848) was not elevated to the baronetcy until 1810. Thomas was a member of Parliament, partner in the firm Baring Brothers & Co. from 1804, and chairman of the London and Southwestern Railroad from 1832 to 1833. Baring Brothers & Co. brokered the $15 million Louisiana Purchase in 1802, which doubled the size of the United States and financially refueled Napoleon’s war effort. Thomas wears a dark blue coat with brass buttons, white waistcoat with a high white collar, bow, and frill down the front, all of which was standard attire for British gentlemen at the turn of the century. His hair is worn à l’antique (hair cut short and worn in curls, especially around the forehead), a style sported by men after the turn of the century that evokes the coiffures of statesmen of ancient Rome. The back of the frame contains plaited brown hair. There is a small area of pigment loss located at the lower right edge of the sitter’s coat.

results.title: Shades of Greene : one generation of an English family
results.creator: Lewis, Jeremy
description: xii, 575 pages, 16 unnumbered pages of plates : 20 cm

"Graham Greene was one of the great writers of the last century, as well as enjoying a varied and adventurous career as a secret agent, traveller, publisher and man of letters: but he was not the only member of the Greene family to lead an extraordinary life. Of the twelve children born to brothers Charles and Edward Greene, eight recorded remarkable achievements - from a BBC Director General to an Everest mountaineer, from a female MI6 agent to a champion of Communist China, from a founder of a far-right political party to the inevitable black sheep - and in documenting the interlacing lives of this generation, Lewis provides both a fascinating exercise in group biography and a masterly account of English society in the twentieth century."--Back cover
Originally published: London: Jonathan Cape, 2010

results.title: Portrait of Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey, née Lamack
results.creator: John I Smart (British, 1741–1811)
description: Portrait of Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey, née Lamack, c. 1776. John I Smart (British, 1741–1811). Graphite and wash on laid paper in a modern gold frame; framed: 6.2 x 5.3 cm (2 7/16 x 2 1/16 in.); unframed: 5.8 x 4.8 cm (2 5/16 x 1 7/8 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Edward B. Greene Collection 1942.1155
Sketches helped John Smart work out the particulars of a portrait before commencing the miniature on ivory, and they were useful in the event that a duplicate might later be required.

Although it is impossible to say if it was always part of the artist’s process to execute a preparatory sketch prior to painting each miniature, we do know that John Smart retained many hundreds of these sketches. A group of preparatory sketches—of which this portrait is one—descended through the Smirke family after Smart’s daughter Sarah gave a sketchbook containing preparatory portrait studies to her friend Mary Smirke, sister of the celebrated Victorian architect Sydney Smirke. This book was probably broken up around 1877 when it was divided between Sydney’s daughters Mary Jemmett and Mrs. Lange, whose portions were both sold at auction in 1928. Compared to his contemporaries George Engleheart (1752–1829) and Andrew Plimer (1763–1837), whose female sitters were often painted in similar simple white gowns, Smart often lavished more attention on the costumes in his portraits of women, whose dresses incorporated colored silks, printed fabrics, and luxury trimmings like lace and fur, as seen in this portrait. Mrs. Bailey wears a violet surcoat trimmed with fur, worn over a cream-colored gown trimmed with a border of alternating pearls and blue stones and two vertical rows of pearls with one large pearl between them. Her brown hair is dressed high with ringlets descending down her neck and over her shoulders. The coiffure is ornamented with a strand of pearls and two ostrich plumes. The case is modern, and there is a brownish cast to what was originally pale, cream-colored paper—the result of light exposure changing the color over time. Smart’s preparatory sketches were compiled in books but once removed were often grouped in frames or placed in lockets such as this one. This portrait was part of the Smirke collection owned by Mary Jemmett, who sold it at Christie’s, London, on February 29, 1928. Lot 61 for this sale is described as “Mrs. Bailey, wearing pale mauve and white dress, her hair dressed high and trimmed with feathers.” The sitter, Mrs. Nathaniel Bailey (née Lamack), of Clapham, married the member of Parliament for Abingdon on March 18, 1773. Her husband was of sufficient means and is recorded in 1775 as having performed his annual distribution of £100 of bread and meat to the poor of his borough. Little else is known about this sitter. This drawing was a preparatory study for a portrait on ivory, signed and dated 1776, and measuring 2 inches high. The ivory miniature was formerly in the Ashcroft collection and was sold at Sotheby’s, London, in May 1946 to Arthur Jaffé, having previously been on loan to the Victoria and Albert Museum from 1924 to 1939. In this sale the miniature is described as “An Attractive Miniature of a Lady, by John Smart, signed and dated 1776, head and gaze three-quarters dexter, a white feather and pearls in her high piled chestnut hair, ringlets falling to the shoulders, wearing a pearl and emerald bordered low-cut cream dress and fur trimmed lavender jacket.” It most recently sold at Christie’s, London, in 2003. This portrait miniature is identical to the preparatory sketch here, both of which describe the sitter as wearing a faintly violet costume, though this color is no longer discernible in the sketch. The current location of the miniature on ivory is unknown. Edward Greene donated this and nine other preparatory studies by Smart to the Cleveland Museum of Art in 1941 and 1942. This sketch was acquired by Greene from Leopold Davis for around $260 in 1930. Although this portrait was probably part of the same sketchbook as the other nine purchased by Greene, Davis did not indicate whether or not this was indeed the case. The majority of these sketches were in a compromised condition, with fading and foxing especially prevalent.

results.title: Portrait of a Woman, called Mrs. Close
results.creator: Horace Hone (British, 1756–1825)
description: Portrait of a Woman, called Mrs. Close, 1786. Horace Hone (British, 1756–1825). Watercolor on ivory in an ormolu frame; framed: 8.9 x 7.5 cm (3 1/2 x 2 15/16 in.); sight: 6.5 x 5.2 cm (2 9/16 x 2 1/16 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, The Edward B. Greene Collection 1943.644
The artist, Horace Hone, signed the miniature in the lower right with the monogram HH.

The sitter of this portrait has been called “Mrs. Close” at least from 1929, when Edward Greene purchased the miniature from the dealer Leo Schidlof. The reason for this identification is, however, unknown, as there is no inscribed reference to Mrs. Close on the miniature or any of its supporting materials. Like so many of Horace Hone’s female sitters, her gown and hair are ornamented with strands of pearls, and she is set against an olive green background. Her brown, curly hair falls over her shoulders, dressed high with a pearl ornament on the right side. She has large, dark brown eyes and rosy cheeks and wears a plum-colored dress with a lace fichu around the neckline. The sitter also dons a miniature with the portrait turned toward her chest, exposing the back, which is ornamented with plaited hair. It is noteworthy that the miniature appears this way; even if it had been facing forward, its portrait would not have been legible to the viewer. The decision to place the back foremost underscores the highly private nature of the miniature portrait and its significance for the sitter, who was perhaps accustomed to wearing her miniature with the portrait turned toward her body. This manner of wearing miniatures was adopted by both men and women and was a popular vignette in sentimental novels and poems of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.

results.creator: North Virginia Community College
results.description: Congratulations to our Summer 2024, Fall 2024 and Spring 2025 graduates! Please enjoy our 2025 Commencement Ceremony @nvcc streamed live at the George Mason University Eagle Bank Arena. 00:00 Start 41:45 Welcome 44:47 NVCC Class of 2025 Procession 1:22:30 Commencement Guest Speaker Hannah Williams is a social activist and entrepreneur tackling a major issue: salary transparency. After realizing she was being significantly underpaid as a data analyst, Hannah founded @SalaryTransparentStreet a video series where she interviews strangers about their jobs and their pay. Her goal for the series was to help workers learn and earn more, and that happened — on a big scale! In fact, Hannah now has 3 million followers on social media, including TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and LinkedIn. Hannah has testified in support of pay transparency bills in Virginia, Maryland and D.C., and her work has been featured by major media organizations including The Washington Post, TIME and BBC News. She was named a Money.com Changemaker in 2023, and she made the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2024. After graduating from NOVA in 2017 with an A.S. in business administration, Hannah transferred to Georgetown University where she earned her bachelor's degree in management. results.title: Scattered Light from Close-in Extrasolar Planets: Prospects of Detection with the MOST Satellite
creator: Daniel Green
Jaymie Matthews
Sara Seager
Rainer Kuschnig
results.description: The ultra-precise photometric space satellite MOST (Microvariability and Oscillations of STars) will provide the first opportunity to measure the albedos and scattered light curves from known short-period extrasolar planets. Due to the changing phases of an extrasolar planet as it orbits its parent star, the combined light of the planet-star system will vary on the order of tens of micromagnitudes. The amplitude and shape of the resulting light curve is sensitive to the planet's radius and orbital inclination, as well as the composition and size distribution of the scattering particles in the planet's atmosphere. To predict the capabilities of MOST and other planned space missions, we have constructed a series of models of such light curves, improving upon earlier work by incorporating more realistic details such as: limb darkening of the star, intrinsic granulation noise in the star itself, tidal distortion and back-heating, higher angular resolution of the light scattering from the planet, and exploration of the significance of the angular size of the star as seen from the planet. We use photometric performance simulations of the MOST satellite, with the light curve models as inputs, for one of the mission's primary targets, $\tau$ Bo\"otis. These simulations demonstrate that, even adopting a very conservative signal detection limit of 4.2 $\mu$mag in amplitude (not power), we will be able to either detect the $\tau$ Bo\"otis planet light curve or put severe constraints on possible extrasolar planet atmospheric models.

results.title: Testing Split Supersymmetry with Inflation
creator: Nathaniel Craig
Daniel Green
results.description: Split supersymmetry (SUSY) -- in which SUSY is relevant to our universe but largely inaccessible at current accelerators -- has become increasingly plausible given the absence of new physics at the LHC, the success of gauge coupling unification, and the observed Higgs mass. Indirect probes of split SUSY such as electric dipole moments (EDMs) and flavor violation offer hope for further evidence but are ultimately limited in their reach. Inflation offers an alternate window into SUSY through the direct production of superpartners during inflation. These particles are capable of leaving imprints in future cosmological probes of primordial non-gaussianity. Given the recent observations of BICEP2, the scale of inflation is likely high enough to probe the full range of split SUSY scenarios and therefore offers a unique advantage over low energy probes. The key observable for future experiments is equilateral non-gaussianity, which will be probed by both cosmic microwave background (CMB) and large scale structure (LSS) surveys. In the event of a detection, we forecast our ability to find evidence for superpartners through the scaling behavior in the squeezed limit of the bispectrum.

results.title: Is There Scale-Dependent Bias in Single-Field Inflation?
creator: Roland de Putter
Olivier Doré
Daniel Green
results.description: Scale-dependent halo bias due to local primordial non-Gaussianity provides a strong test of single-field inflation. While it is universally understood that single-field inflation predicts negligible scale-dependent bias compared to current observational uncertainties, there is still disagreement on the exact level of scale-dependent bias at a level that could strongly impact inferences made from future surveys. In this paper, we clarify this confusion and derive in various ways that there is exactly zero scale-dependent bias in single-field inflation. Much of the current confusion follows from the fact that single-field inflation does predict a mode coupling of matter perturbations at the level of $f_{NL}^{loc} \approx -5/3$, which naively would lead to scale-dependent bias. However, we show explicitly that this mode coupling cancels out when perturbations are evaluated at a fixed physical scale rather than fixed coordinate scale. Furthermore, we show how the absence of scale-dependent bias can be derived easily in any gauge. This result can then be incorporated into a complete description of the observed galaxy clustering, including the previously studied general relativistic terms, which are important at the same level as scale-dependent bias of order $f_{NL}^{loc} \sim 1$. This description will allow us to draw unbiased conclusions about inflation from future galaxy clustering data.

results.title: In The Warlords’ Shadow: Special Operations Forces, The Afghans, And Their Fight Against The Taliban
results.creator: Westminster Institute
results.description: In the Warlords’ Shadow: Special Operations Forces, the Afghans, and Their Fight Against the Taliban (Daniel Green, April 4, 2018) Transcript available below About the speaker Dr. Daniel R. Green  is a Defense Fellow at The Washington Institute for Near East Policy focusing on counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency, and stability operations in the Middle East and Central Asia. He is a reserve officer with the U.S. Navy and most recently served in Iraq (2015-2016) as a tribal and political engagement officer in Baghdad. His prior deployments include service in Afghanistan (2012) as a tribal and political engagement officer in Uruzgan province; as the International Security Assistance Force Joint Command liaison officer to the U.S. Embassy’s Office of Interagency Provincial Affairs in Afghanistan (2009-2010); as a tribal and political engagement officer in Fallujah, Iraq (2007); and as a civilian with the Department of State as the political advisor to the Tarin Kowt Provincial Reconstruction Team in Uruzgan province, Afghanistan (2005-2006). Since 2001, he has held several senior advisory positions dealing with the Middle East, Central Asia, and NATO/Europe in the Office of the Secretary of Defense and the State Department. Dr. Green has received the State Department’s Superior Honor Award and the U.S. Army’s Superior Civilian Honor Award for his work in Afghanistan, and was also personally commended by then-chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Peter Pace. He is a recipient of the Office of the Secretary of Defense’s Exceptional Public Service Award. His first book,  The Valley’s Edge: A Year with the Pashtuns in the Heartland of the Taliban , was published by Potomac Books in 2011; his second, co-authored with Brig. Gen. William F. Mullen, III, USMC,  Fallujah Redux: The Anbar Awakening and the Struggle with al-Qaeda , was published by Naval Institute Press in 2014.  His third book,  In the Warlords’ Shadow: Special Operations Forces, the Afghans, and their Fight with the Taliban , will be published by Naval Institute Press in July 2017. He recently contributed a chapter titled “Organizing like the Enemy: Special Operations Forces, Afghan Culture, and Village Stability Operations” to an edited volume titled  Our Latest Longest War: Losing Hearts and Minds in Afghanistan  by Aaron O’Connell, published by the University of Chicago Press in April 2017. For more on Afghanistan, see Ambassador Ali Jalali’s Westminster talk:  Afghanistan: From the Great Game to the Global War on Terror  and Hassan Abbas’s Westminster talk:  The Taliban Revival: Violence and Extremism on the Pakistan-Afghanistan Frontier .

results.title: Dr. Dan Green on Mental Health and Leading Men Well
results.creator: International Church of Monrovia
results.description: Today on the No Regrets Podcast, Nate Gruber is joined by Dr. Dan Green, Clinical Director of New Life Resources and a long-time partner of No Regrets, for an important conversation on the mental health of the men we lead—and the men we are becoming. Dr. Green brings practical insight for leaders who feel stuck or are facing roadblocks in their own lives or on their teams. As mental health becomes more widely discussed, many men are still unsure what to do with what they're feeling. Labels can sometimes increase isolation rather than bring clarity, especially when men struggle to express their needs. results.title: A New Target for Cosmic Axion Searches
creator: Daniel Baumann
Daniel Green
Benjamin Wallisch
results.description: Future CMB experiments have the potential to probe the density of relativistic species at the sub-percent level. Sensitivity at this level allows light thermal relics to be detected up to arbitrarily high decoupling temperatures. Conversely, the absence of a detection would require extra light species never to have been in equilibrium with the Standard Model. In this paper, we exploit this feature to demonstrate the sensitivity of future cosmological observations to the couplings of axions to all of the Standard Model degrees of freedom. In many cases, the constraints achievable from cosmology will surpass existing bounds from laboratory experiments and astrophysical observations by orders of magnitude.

results.title: Reheating Closed String Inflation
results.creator: Daniel Green
results.description: Protecting the inflationary potential from quantum corrections typically requires symmetries that constrain the form of couplings of the inflaton to other sectors. We will explore how these restrictions affect reheating in models with UV completions. In particular, we look at how reheating occurs when inflation is governed by closed strings, using N-flation as an example. We find that coupling the inflaton preferentially to the Standard Model is difficult, and hidden sectors are typically reheated. Observational constraints are only met by a fraction of the models. In some working models, relativistic relics in the hidden sector provide dark matter candidates with masses that range from keV to PeV, with lighter masses being preferred.

results.title: Equilateral Non-Gaussianity and New Physics on the Horizon
creator: Daniel Baumann
Daniel Green
results.description: We examine the effective theory of single-field inflation in the limit where the scalar perturbations propagate with a small speed of sound. In this case the non-linearly realized time-translation symmetry of the Lagrangian implies large interactions, giving rise to primordial non-Gaussianities. When the non-Gaussianities are measurable, these interactions will become strongly coupled unless new physics appears close to the Hubble scale. Due to its proximity to the Hubble scale, the new physics is not necessarily decoupled from inflationary observables and can potentially affect the predictions of the model. To understand the types of corrections that may arise, we construct weakly-coupled completions of the theory and study their observational signatures.

results.title: DVD Transfer 217 (NBA on NBC: 1994 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals - Chicago Bulls at New York Knicks: Game 7 - Partial Recording)
results.creator: NBA Entertainment; NBC Sports-NBCUniversal/Comcast; WEAU-Gray Media
results.description: (c)1994 NBA Entertainment; NBC Sports-NBCUniversal/Comcast and WEAU-Gray Media So, this came as a bonus DVD recording alongside Game 7 of the 1990 Eastern Conference Finals I posted a while back. However, I had a much more difficult time ripping the video for this one (and had actually given up on this one not that long ago) before deciding to give it one more try last week. DVD Transfer 217 contains a mostly-complete (unfortunately, it appears that the original recorder's tape ran out with a few minutes left in the game) recording of Game 7 of the 1994 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals involving the biggest rivalry of the early 1990s between the three-time defending NBA champion Chicago Bulls (55-27 and the #3 seed) and the Atlantic Division champion New York Knicks (tied with the Central Division champion Atlanta Hawks for the Eastern Conference's best record at 57-25). Entering the 1993-94 season; the Knicks (who had no draft picks in 1993 after their lone pick was traded to Orlando) had faced the Bulls in the post-season in each of the three previous playoffs and had been eliminated each time (including the 1992 Eastern Conference Semi-Finals where the series went the full 7 games before Chicago advanced and the 1993 Eastern Conference Finals where the Knicks - with the conference's best record - were eliminated in 6 games) and were seeking their first trip to the Finals since 1973. Changes to the Pat Riley-led Knicks included the off-season arrival of Sacramento Kings forward Anthony Bonner and a mid-season trade that saw the Knicks trade guard Tony Campbell and their 1st round pick in 1997 to the lowly Dallas Mavericks in exchange for point guard Derek Harper (picked up after starting point guard Doc Rivers suffered a season-ending knee injury early in the year); while late in the regular-season longtime owner Paramount sold both the team and the Madison Square Garden arena to Viacom (which eventually sold the team to a consortium of ITT and Cablevision; with Cablevision currently being the sole owner), advancing to this series by ousting the (then-)New Jersey Nets 3-1 in the first round. Meanwhile; the Chicago Bulls entered the 1993-94 season seeking to become the first team in any professional sport since the Boston Celtics of the 1960s to win a 4th consecutive championship (the Celtics winning 8 consecutive NBA titles between 1959-66) but just before the season were rocked by the sudden retirement of Michael Jordan just over two months after the July 23, 1993 murder of his father James (whose body wasn't discovered until 10 days later, with the assailants - Daniel Green and Larry Martin Demery - eventually being convicted and sentenced to life in prison), eventually deciding to try his hand at baseball with the Birmingham Barons, a minor-league team affiliated with the Chicago White Sox (incidentally also owned by Bulls owner Jerry Reinsdorf). Other changes to the Bulls roster included the drafting of rookie forward Corie Blount along with the signing of journeyman shooting guard Pete Myers (Myers, who replaced Jordan at shooting guard, had most recently played in Italy), former Sacramento Kings center (but having also most recently played in Italy) Bill Wennington and point guard Steve Kerr (late of the Orlando Magic) as well as Croatian forward Toni Kukoc (who the Bulls had drafted in 1990) making his NBA debut while during the season backup center Stacey King was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for Australian-born center Luc Longley. The Bulls entered the playoffs with a 3-0 sweep of frequent post-season rival Cleveland Cavaliers (the 3rd and final game being the last game played at Richfield Coliseum before the Cavs moved to Gund Arena {now Rocket Arena}). This would be a closely-fought series (with the home team emerging victorious in each game) that included Kukoc making the game-winning 23-foot buzzer-beater shot in Game 3 for a 104-102 Bulls win to make the series 2-1 (Kukoc's shot being made possible in part after Scottie Pippen - who replaced Jordan as the Bulls' main offensive threat - refused to enter the game due to being upset with Phil Jackson drawing up the last play of the game for Kukoc while Pippen would inbound; that game also included a fight between Derek Harper and Bulls guard Jo Jo English that spilled into the stands - with NBA Commissioner David Stern in attendance); an 87-86 Knicks victory in Game 5 noted by a questionable call by Hue Hollins, who determined that Pippen had fouled Knicks guard Hubert Davis, who sank both free throws for what proved the winning points and a Game 6 Chicago victory at Chicago Stadium 93-79 (the biggest margin of victory for either team in the series) noted for Pippen dunking on Knicks center Patrick Ewing. Game 7 would be a closely fought battle with the Knicks leading 22-19 at the end of the 1st, 38-37 at halftime and 67-63 at the end of the 3rd quarter before pulling away in the fourth to dethrone the three-time defending NBA champion Bulls 87-77. Calling the action for NBC are - as per usual - Marv Albert (who when he wasn't on the clock for NBC was also working games for the Knicks on the MSG cable network) and former Orlando Magic head coach Matt Goukas (who left shortly after the 1993 draft) and sideline reporter Ahmad Rashad; while NBA Showtime host Bob Costas hosted NBC's coverage (which including an airing of the 1994 NBA Draft Lottery during halftime) NOTES 1. For the Bulls, Scottie Pippen led the team with 20 points, 5 assists and 16 rebounds (albeit with 3 turnovers and making only 8 of his 22 field goal attempts), while Horace Grant added 17 points and 4 boards (but also 5 fouls), Pete Myers adding 15 points and 4 rebounds (and also 4 fouls); with the only significant reserve support coming from Toni Kukoc (9 points, 4 rebounds). 2. For the Knicks; four of their starters finished in double figures in points (the exception being point guard Derek Harper with 6 points). Patrick Ewing led the way with 18 points, 17 rebounds, 6 assists and a block; while Charles Oakley (who began his career with the Bulls before moving to the Big Apple in 1988 in a trade with Bill Cartwright) added 17 points and a game-high 20 rebounds. John Starks added 10 points and 3 assists (though shooting an abysmal 2-for-11) while Charles Smith (whose claim to NBA notoriety was his having a potential game-winning shot blocked 4 times in Game 5 of the previous year's Eastern Conference Finals) added 11 points and 2 blocks. Bench support came from Anthony Mason (9 points, 5 rebounds), Hubert Davis (8 points) and Greg Anthony (7 points). 3. The Bulls' defeat meant that Game 6 was the final game played at Chicago Stadium, with both the Bulls and the NHL's Chicago Blackhawks both moving across the street to the United Center (where they remain as of 2025) and the old stadium being torn down between February and May 1995. 4. The Bulls' defeat also marked the final game with Chicago for a number of players connected to their (first) three-peat, including center Bill Cartwright (dealt to Seattle for his final season), power forward Horace Grant (who jumped ship to the rapidly improving Magic), center Scott Williams (who left for the lowly Philadelphia 76ers), guard Jo Jo English (who went to the CBA's Pittsburgh Piranhas) and point guard John Paxson (Paxson - who missed most of the season due to injury - announced his retirement soon after) 5. As for the Knicks, they found themselves facing a surprising strong challenge in the Eastern Conference Finals from the Indiana Pacers, who pushed New York the full 7 once again (including a Game 5 93-86 Pacers victory remembered for Reggie Miller scoring 25 points in the 4th quarter) before the Knicks emerged victorious with a 94-90 victory in Game 7 (remembered for Patrick Ewing making the game-clinching dunk with 26.9 seconds left to play). That set up an NBA Finals match with the Houston Rockets (seeking not just their first NBA title {having lost to the Celtics in both 1981 and 1986} but also to remove the legacy of the city's sports teams as choke artists {first with the NFL's Houston Oilers blowing leads in three consecutive playoff games - most infamously blowing a 35-3 lead early in the 3rd quarter in the 1992 AFC Wild-Card Game to the Buffalo Bills, who won 41-38 in overtime in what became known as "The Comeback" - as well as the Rockets falling behind 0-2 to the Phoenix Suns in the Western Conference Semi-Finals that led to the Houston Chronicle's "Choke City" headline before rallying to win that series in 7 games and leading to the "Clutch City" nickname}). That series would also go the full 7 (meaning that, since the first round was a Best-of-5 at the time, had the Nets won one more game against the Knicks in their first round meeting, New York would have played a maximum of 26 playoff games) - with the Knicks leading 3-2 after their 91-84 win in Game 5 on June 17 (a game overshadowed by the O.J. Simpson chase in which the former Buffalo Bills legend and NBC sportscaster was involved in a chase - in a white Ford Bronco owned by Simpson's one-time Bills teammate Al Cowlings - with the L.A.P.D. after Simpson was charged with the murders of estranged wife Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman before the Juice surrendered; eventually being acquitted {though later held liable in civil court} following a trial that was less a criminal trial and more a media circus) before the Rockets - seeking their first title in a still-existing league (the city's most recent championship being the Houston Aeros in 1975 with the old World Hockey Association) - won their last 2 games (including a 86-84 win in Game 6 which saw Rockets center Hakeem Olajuwon blocking a potential game-winning 3-pointer by John Starks; with a rattled Starks making only 2 of 18 shots in the deciding Game 7) to clinch their first NBA championship (and in the process denying New York City a chance to celebrate both an NBA and NHL championship, as between Games 3 and 4 of the NBA Finals the New York Rangers won their first Stanley Cup since 1940 as well as making Knicks head coach Pat Riley the only coach to lose 2 Game 7's in the NBA Finals with different teams {the first being when Riley's Lakers were defeated by the Celtics in Game 7 of the 1984 NBA Finals; while had the Knicks won Game 7 he would have been the first coach to win 2 Game 7's in the Finals with different teams - the first would have been with the Lakers in Game 7 in 1988})

results.title: SpaceWarZ
results.description: "SpaceWarZ is a two-player game. Each player tries to destroy the other player's ship, without getting his own ship destroyed. If you destroy the other player's ship, your score goes up by one; the first player to reach the agreed-upon high score wins the game. Ships can rotate and they can accelerate by using their engines. If the gravity option is being used, then ships can also move by being attracted to the sun (or black hole, if it is present). The game tries to realistically simulate motion, such that if you accelerate forwards for five seconds, its going to take another five seconds of acceleration in the opposite direction to stop your motion. Each ship can fire bullets. Each player can have up to five bullets in action at once. Bullets travel for approximately 2/3 of the horizontal length of the window before they self-destruct. A ship can be destroyed by being hit by a bullet (even by one of your own bullets!), by being sucked into the sun or a black hole, or by ramming into the other player's ship."

results.title: Alexandria City Council Legislative Meeting - October 13, 2026
results.creator: OpenPublica
results.description: # Alexandria City Council Legislative Meeting - October 13, 2026 The Alexandria City Council held its regular legislative meeting on October 13, 2026, beginning with a Landmark Community Development Authority board meeting at 6:02 PM, followed by an executive session and the public legislative session at approximately 7:00 PM. The meeting included three proclamations, oral reports on regional transportation and local preparedness, a state of the economy presentation from the Alexandria Economic Development Partnership (AEDP), a state of 911 presentation, approval of consent items, contested appointments to boards and commissions, and establishment of a friendship city relationship with Osijek, Croatia. ### Consent Calendar - Approved the Landmark CDA meeting minutes from October 14, 2025. - Approved the amended 2026 Special Assessment Roll with a zero annual revenue requirement due to capitalized interest and incremental tax revenues. - Approved the electronic participation resolution for the City Council (roll-call vote: all ayes). - Approved the resolution to convene in closed executive session under VA Code § 2.2-3711(A)(6) (roll-call vote: all ayes). - Approved the resolution regarding the closed executive session (roll-call vote: all ayes). - Approved Roll-Call Consent Items 12–20 (receipt of resignations, uncontested appointments, meeting minutes of Sept. 8, 19, 22, and Oct. 2, 2026, and several grant awards and the monthly financial report) (roll-call vote: all ayes). - Approved the City Council schedule (voice vote: all ayes). ### Public Comments & Testimony - No public comments were taken during the meeting. Written statements were accepted by the City Clerk. ### Proclamations and Recognitions - **Ben Brenman Award (Oct. 13, 2026):** Councilman Chapman read a proclamation honoring the Friends of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Cemetery and the Social Responsibility Group for their preservation and stewardship of the Douglass Memorial Cemetery, the largest African American cemetery in Alexandria. The award was presented by the Alexandria Archaeological Commission. Recipients spoke about the restoration work and plans to nominate the entire Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex for the National Historic Register. The proclamation passed unanimously. - **40th Anniversary of Tenants and Workers United (TWU):** Councilman Elnoubi read a proclamation celebrating TWU's founding in 1986 and its advocacy for living wages, rental assistance, restorative practices in schools, and anti-displacement policies. Councilman Aguirre (participating virtually) and Mayor Gaskins praised TWU's organizing and partnership. The proclamation passed unanimously. - **National Breast Cancer Awareness Month:** Councilwoman Greene read a proclamation declaring October 2026 as Breast Cancer Awareness Month in Alexandria. Speakers included Coco McLean (one-year triple-negative breast cancer survivor), Rose Dawson (library director), and Charlotte Hall (Breast Cancer Collective). The proclamation passed unanimously. ### Oral Reports - **Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC) – Councilman Elnoubi:** Reported continued discussion on lithium-ion battery safety and disposal, noting a gap in safe, affordable disposal paths for damaged or recalled batteries. He requested guidance to the city manager to convene a work group and develop a coordinated plan. - **Northern Virginia Transportation Commission (NVTC) – Vice Mayor Bagley and Councilman Aguirre:** Celebrated 10 years of the Commuter Choice program, which has funneled $218 million into transit, saved nearly 2 million hours in traffic, $26 million at the gas pump, and brought $68 million in economic benefit. VRE presented its proposed budget; challenges remain for funding future projects. A DRPT public hearing on a potential consolidation of local bus services (Dash, ART, Fairfax Connector, etc.) is scheduled for October 21, 2026. - **Eisenhower Partnership Board of Directors – Councilwoman Greene:** Highlighted the annual fall breakfast with Director of Planning Paul Stoddard. Next meeting is October 16, 2026. - **Citizen Corps Council (CCC) – Councilwoman Greene and Councilwoman Marks:** Reported on National Preparedness Month activities (Tons of Trucks event) and planned bylaw changes to formalize participation of Volunteer Alexandria and the Amateur Radio Club. - **COG Chesapeake Bay Water Resources and Policy Committee – Councilwoman Greene:** Attended the annual retreat focused on policy, resilience, and upcoming General Assembly decisions. - **COG Food and Agricultural Regional Member (FARM) Policy Committee – Councilwoman Greene:** Noted new chair J.D. Spain (Arlington) and reviewed impacts of SNAP and Medicare cuts and the Capital Area Food Bank’s Hunger Report on rising food insecurity. ### City Council General Updates - Councilman Elnoubi requested consensus to direct the city manager to form a work group addressing safe disposal of lithium-ion batteries, including public guidance, handling protocols, and cost options. Vice Mayor Bagley suggested including storage and charging safety recommendations. Consensus was reached. - Other council members reported attending community events: Witter Place Apartments affordable housing ribbon cutting, COG Congressional delegation, Duncan Donuts grand reopening, Old Town Art Festival, Barktoberfest, Ruby Tucker Day, TWU 40th anniversary gala, and the Grand African Run (1,500+ participants). ### Discussion Items - **State of the Economy (AEDP):** AEDP President Marian D. and Vice President Christina Mindrop presented the FY26 mid-year market report. Key statistics: - 2,791 jobs created, 650,000+ square feet retained/occupied, 27 active projects. - Office vacancy fell from 21.6% to 18.8% year-over-year; net absorption remained negative at -160,000 sq ft. - Potomac Yard has zero office vacancy due to fully occupied built-to-suit spaces, but demand from tenants wanting proximity to Virginia Tech is unmet. Landlords are building speculative suites in Old Town and Carlyle. - AEDP secured $4.13 million in competitive state funding for innovation ecosystem, including $800,000 for the Alexandria Innovation Lab. - Councilmembers discussed challenges in Potomac Yard (Councilman Chapman expressed concern about lack of available office space) and the need to preserve flexible industrial/warehouse space in Eisenhower Corridor. - **State of 911:** Director Renee Gordon (DEC) reported that for FY26 so far, DEC handled 72,000 911 calls (total call volume 311,000), with 94% answered within 15 seconds (national standard). The center was the first in the region to obtain CALEA accreditation. Gordon announced her retirement at the end of October. Councilmembers praised her leadership and the culture of calmness she built. ### Key Outcomes - **Votes on Proclamations:** All three proclamations passed unanimously. - **Consent Agenda:** Approved unanimously by roll-call vote. - **Appointment of Viewer (Item 21):** Postponed indefinitely by unanimous roll-call vote because the original viewer submitted a late report, rendering the item moot. - **Friendship City with Osijek, Croatia (Item 22):** Resolution approved unanimously by roll-call vote. - **Contested Appointments (Items 23–37):** The majority vote-getters were approved by roll-call vote (all ayes). Winners include: - Alexandria Gang Prevention Community Task Force: Tori Golden - Transportation Commission: Timothy Levane and Stephen McBride - Archaeological Commission: Don Helby - Beautification Commission: Sibylle Braum - Board of Zoning Appeals: Anne Newman - Children, Youth and Families Collaborative Commission: Catherine Klinger - Commission for the Arts: Stacey Becker - Commission for Women: Holly Davis - Commission on Aging: Denise Wright (representative of older persons) and Daniel Green (citizen member 60+) - Commission on Persons with Disabilities: Darren Marquot - Community Services Board: Sabrine Bruno - Park and Recreation Commission: Robert Moore - Potomac Yard Design Advisory Committee: Bradley Hinocheston - Public Health Advisory Commission: Lori Hughes - Public Records Advisory Commission: Rachel Townsend - **Council Schedule:** Approved, with additions of the DRPT hearing (Oct. 21) and Croatian Embassy event (Oct. 19). - **Directive to City Manager:** To form a work group on lithium-ion battery disposal, with a report back at a future meeting. ### Next Steps - The DRPT public hearing on bus consolidation will be held October 21, 2026; public comment period open until October 23, 2026. - The city manager will convene the lithium-ion battery work group and report back. - Renee Gordon retires at the end of October 2026; deputy director Tunisia Wells will assume leadership.
